By Jamie Martin

Agricultural leadership and collaboration were celebrated at the 2026 National Association of State Departments of Agriculture (NASDA) annual meeting in Portland, Maine. The organization honored an industry leader and a major agricultural company for their efforts to strengthen agriculture and support state agriculture departments across the country.

One of the event's highest honors, the Bill Northey Legacy Award, was presented to Dave Flakne, Head of State Affairs for Syngenta. The award recognizes individuals outside NASDA who have shown outstanding dedication to promoting the organization's mission and supporting agriculture through service, advocacy, and collaboration.

Flakne has spent decades working alongside agricultural leaders at the local, state, and national levels. Throughout his career, he has built strong relationships within the industry and helped encourage cooperation among organizations focused on supporting farmers and rural economies.

NASDA leaders noted that Flakne's commitment to agriculture has remained strong for many years. His consistent participation in agricultural discussions and events has helped strengthen communication between industry stakeholders and state departments of agriculture. Through thoughtful advocacy and partnership-building, he has contributed to the advancement of shared agricultural priorities.

The award is named in honor of Bill Northey and recognizes individuals who leave a lasting impact on the agricultural sector. By honoring Flakne, NASDA highlighted the value of leadership, dedication, and long-term involvement in addressing agricultural challenges and opportunities.

NASDA also presented its Public-Private Partnership Award to ADM. The award recognizes organizations that successfully partner with state agriculture departments to create programs and initiatives that deliver measurable benefits to agriculture.

ADM received the honor for its involvement in NASDA's 2025 United Kingdom Sustainable Aviation Fuel Inbound Trade Mission. Working alongside state agriculture departments from several Midwestern states, the company helped demonstrate how the agricultural industry contributes to renewable fuel production.

The mission focused on educating policymakers and stakeholders from the United Kingdom about the agricultural feedstock-to-fuel supply chain. Participants gained valuable insights into how crops and other agricultural resources are transformed into renewable energy products that can support sustainability goals.

Through facility visits and discussions with agricultural experts, visitors learned about the important role farming plays in renewable fuel development. The initiative also strengthened international relationships and highlighted opportunities for future collaboration between agricultural and energy sectors.

NASDA recognized ADM for providing access to facilities, sharing technical knowledge, and actively supporting engagement across multiple states. These efforts helped create a successful educational experience while showcasing agricultural innovation and the capabilities of the Midwest's farming industry.

A key contributor to the project was Greg Webb, ADM's Vice President of State Government Relations. With nearly 40 years of experience in the field, Webb helped connect industry leaders, policymakers, and agricultural stakeholders. His efforts played an important role in ensuring the success of the mission and enhancing cooperation among participants.

The awards presented during NASDA's annual meeting demonstrate the importance of partnerships, leadership, and innovation in agriculture. Individuals and organizations that work together can help address industry challenges while creating opportunities for producers and rural communities.

As the agricultural sector continues to evolve, collaboration remains essential. The recognition of Dave Flakne and ADM serves as an example of how leadership, expertise, and teamwork can support growth, sustainability, and long-term success across the agricultural industry.

text:
Advance purchase commitments from AVEVA, Bain & Company, Google, McKinsey, and others support Infinium's Project Atlas, a Texas-based planned facility expected to produce up to 100,000 metric tons of high-integrity sustainable aviation fuel per year.

WASHINGTON, Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Sustainable Aviation Buyers Alliance (SABA) today announced commitments from members to purchase sustainable aviation fuel certificates (SAFc) associated with Infinium Energy's Project Atlas, an eSAF facility expected to produce approximately 100,000 metric tons of SAF annually, providing the long-term structured contracts that are catalytic to securing project financing.

The groundbreaking results of SABA's latest procurement were supported by leading member organizations, including AVEVA, Bain & Company, Google, McKinsey, and others, and mark an important addition to SABA's market model. Through exclusive focus on supporting projects toward final investment decision, this procurement represents a first-ever application of SABA's approach to drive new production of highly scalable, high-integrity SAF. Infinium submitted its winning proposal jointly with American Airlines, which will take physical delivery of the fuel and oversee fuel logistics. Contracted volumes under these agreements are expected to support greenhouse gas abatement of over 212,000 mtCO2e, equivalent to the emissions of over 3,500 JFK to LAX commercial flights.

"Reducing emissions from business travel is an important part of our sustainability efforts," said Isabelle Schuhmann, Global Director of Environmental Sustainability at McKinsey. "By supporting next-generation sustainable aviation fuel, this purchase helps advance a promising solution for decarbonizing aviation at scale, while enabling the travel that is essential to serving our clients."

Aviation currently accounts for approximately 2-3% of global greenhouse gas emissions, yet SAF supply remains limited and at a significant premium to conventional jet fuel. Infinium, which was selected through SABA's procurement process earlier this year, produces ultra-low carbon eSAF at commercial scale using waste CO₂ and renewable energy, converting captured carbon into drop-in aviation fuel compatible with existing aircraft and infrastructure.

"We're proud to partner with SABA members including AVEVA, Bain & Company, Google, McKinsey, and others, as well as American Airlines to bring Infinium Energy's next world scale eSAF facility to life," said Robert Schuetzle, CEO at Infinium. "Their commitment reflects a shared conviction that decarbonizing aviation requires real investment in next-generation supply."

"The companies purchasing SAF certificates through this agreement are demonstrating the leadership needed to help scale a critical solution for aviation," said American's Chief Sustainability Officer Jill Blickstein. "Their commitments broaden participation in the SAF market, support investment in new production and show how customers can work alongside airlines and fuel producers to advance aviation decarbonization."

SABA procurements use a book and claim model that allows corporate customers to invest in SAF and claim the associated environmental benefits, even when the fuel does not flow directly into the planes their employees or freight fly on. Participating companies purchase SAFc, while the corresponding fuel is delivered to an aircraft operator. American Airlines will serve as the physical offtaker for the SAF purchased through this deal and facilitate the allocation of the associated Scope 3 emission reductions to SABA's participating members.

"Next-generation sustainable aviation fuels have tremendous potential to transform aviation," said Sam Israelit, Chief Sustainability Officer at Bain & Company. "High-integrity market mechanisms can help translate corporate demand into the long-term investment signals needed to bring these technologies to commercial scale."

While the SAF market is growing rapidly, more investment is needed, especially for the next generation technologies the aviation sector requires to meet its long-term decarbonization goals. SABA helps accelerate future supply by aggregating SAF demand from corporate buyers and channeling it into offtake agreements with SAFc suppliers who meet rigorous sustainability criteria. SABA's next generation SAF procurement was specifically designed to drive investment into the innovative new technologies needed to bring scalable supply to the market in the years to come.

"Long-term, bankable offtake is often the missing puzzle piece that keeps new SAF plants from getting financed and built," said Kim Carnahan, GMA CEO and Head of SABA Secretariat. "We're thrilled to be working with our SABA members, Infinium, and American Airlines to fill this need and help get more ultra-low carbon aviation fuel to the market."

"We already know innovation can take us much further, faster, but only if we create the conditions for it to scale," said Jon Creyts, CEO of RMI. "Novel technologies are critical to meeting future demand for sustainable aviation fuel, but they will not be operational in time without investments made today. This procurement demonstrates how aggregated, long-term demand can help take promising eSAF projects from idea to reality."

To date, SABA has aggregated $500 million in demand for SAFc from over 35 member companies, driving needed investment toward sustainable aviation fuels. SABA's procurements are supported by robust market infrastructure, including the SAFc Registry, SAFc Accounting and Reporting Guidance, and SABA's Sustainability Framework. Combined, these tools ensure high-integrity transactions across the market. Recent guidance from standard setting organizations, including the Science-based Targets initiative, has recognized environmental attribute certificates from book and claim systems, like SAFc, as a legitimate tool for decarbonizing hard-to-abate value chain emissions.

With the binding, multi-year offtake agreements from SABA customers in hand, Infinium is well positioned to advance to final investment decision and secure financing to build the facility. In addition to serving voluntary customers, Infinium also plans to sell RFNBO compliant eSAF from the facility into European regulatory markets.

"eFuels represent one of the most sustainable pathways to help decarbonize aviation — but they are more expensive to produce," said Fred Krupp, president of Environmental Defense Fund. "Deals like this one prove that high-integrity e-SAF is investable today, not just in theory. The next test is turning early demand signals like SABA's into the long-term policy and financing conditions that will enable e-SAF suppliers to scale beyond a single project."

Plans for SABA's next procurement are already underway, offering future opportunities for companies to purchase and apply SAFc to their climate targets.

About the Sustainable Aviation Buyers Alliance (SABA)

The Sustainable Aviation Buyers Alliance (SABA) is a joint initiative of Environmental Defense Fund, the Center for Green Market Activation (GMA) and RMI focused on accelerating the path to net-zero aviation by driving investment in, and adoption of, high-integrity sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) and supporting companies, airlines, and freight customers in achieving their climate goals. More information on SABA can be found at www.flysaba.org or follow us on LinkedIn.

About Infinium

Infinium is reimagining how the world powers, moves, and computes. Through Infinium Energy™, the company transforms waste carbon into ultra-low carbon eFuels that decarbonize aviation, industry, and transport. Through Infinium Edge™, Infinium advances next-generation thermal infrastructure for data centers, removing heat as a constraint to enable more efficient, high-performance computing. Grounded in deep chemistry and energy systems expertise, Infinium's platforms turn carbon and heat from limits into opportunities.

American Airlines is a premium global airline connecting more of the U.S. to the world. With roots tracing back to an air mail carrier in the Midwestern United States in 1926, American now operates more than 6,000 daily flights to more than 350 destinations in more than 60 countries and serves more than 200 million customers annually. Powered by a proud and talented team of 130,000 aviation professionals, American's team lives out the airline's purpose of caring for people on life's journey every day.

title: Climeworks, Japan Airlines (JAL) Sign 'First' CORSIA-Compliant Carbon Removal Deal
description:
JAL Targets CORSIA-Compliant Carbon Removals Under the agreement, Climeworks Solutions will source a portfolio of carbon removal projects that are selected to meet ICAO requirements for CORSIA Eligible Emissions Units.
JAL will also buy separate carbon removal credits from Climeworks’ direct air capture operations.
That makes the JAL deal different from a standard corporate carbon removal purchase.
JAL and Climeworks call this deal the world’s first CORSIA-compliant carbon removal purchase agreement.
For carbon removal developers, the opportunity is to produce projects that meet increasingly detailed regulatory requirements.
text:
Japan Airlines (JAL) has signed a carbon removal deal with Climeworks Solutions that the companies describe as the world’s first designed to meet the requirements of the International Civil Aviation Organization’s (ICAO) Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA).

The deal is a new step for carbon removals in aviation. It combines several types of carbon removal with additional direct air capture (DAC) credits from Climeworks.

The companies, however, did not disclose the value or volume of credits covered by the deal. JAL and Climeworks said their research found no earlier purchase agreements of this type.

The deal comes as airlines face growing pressure to cut emissions. Airlines are working on aircraft efficiency, better operations, and sustainable aviation fuel (SAF). Carbon removals can help address emissions that remain after these measures.

JAL Targets CORSIA-Compliant Carbon Removals

Under the agreement, Climeworks Solutions will source a portfolio of carbon removal projects that are selected to meet ICAO requirements for CORSIA Eligible Emissions Units.

The portfolio will include methods such as soil carbon sequestration and biochar. JAL will also buy separate carbon removal credits from Climeworks’ direct air capture operations. This matters because CORSIA has specific rules for which carbon credits airlines can use.

Not every carbon credit in the voluntary carbon market qualifies for CORSIA. ICAO reviews carbon credit programs against requirements covering environmental and social integrity.

Approved programs and eligible unit types can then supply emissions units for specific CORSIA compliance periods. That makes the JAL deal different from a standard corporate carbon removal purchase.

However, the companies’ wording matters. They describe the agreement as a purchase of carbon removal credits designed to meet CORSIA requirements. The announcement does not give a specific number of credits that have already been canceled against a CORSIA obligation.

Why CORSIA Could Reshape Aviation’s Carbon Market

CORSIA is ICAO’s global system for addressing CO₂ emissions from international aviation. The system requires covered airlines to cancel eligible emissions units against their calculated offsetting requirements.

CORSIA began its pilot phase in 2021 and entered its first phase in 2024. Its second phase starts in 2027 and runs through 2035. For 2024–2035, ICAO sets the sector-wide baseline for offsetting at 85% of 2019 emissions from international aviation covered by CORSIA.

Airlines can reduce their CORSIA obligations through eligible fuels and other measures. They can meet remaining requirements by canceling CORSIA Eligible Emissions Units approved by ICAO. This creates potential demand for carbon credits that meet CORSIA’s eligibility rules.

ICAO currently lists eight programs approved to supply eligible emissions units for the 2024–2026 first phase. They include the American Carbon Registry, Architecture for REDD+ Transactions, Climate Action Reserve, Global Carbon Council, Gold Standard, Isometric, the Premium Thailand Voluntary Emission Reduction Program, and Verra’s Verified Carbon Standard.

However, approval of a program does not mean every credit from that program can be used. Individual credits depend on several factors. These include the program, project activity, methodology, vintage, and other conditions.

SEE MORE: CORSIA Could Face a 125 Million Carbon Credit Gap Before 2028, Says Sylvera

Carbon Removals Enter Aviation’s Compliance Pipeline

The JAL-Climeworks agreement also shows how the carbon market is changing. For years, most corporate demand for carbon removals came from the voluntary carbon market. Companies bought removals to address residual emissions or support longer-term climate goals. Regulatory systems are now creating another potential source of demand.

Climeworks launched its compliance-focused Solutions offering in July 2026. The service helps companies find carbon removal portfolios. These portfolios work with frameworks like CORSIA, Article 6.2 of the Paris Agreement, and the EU’s Carbon Removal and Carbon Farming Certification Framework.

The JAL agreement is the first major deal publicly announced by Climeworks under this expanded strategy. For the carbon removal industry, the importance of the deal goes beyond the number of credits sold.

It shows how developers and buyers can build carbon removal portfolios around a specific compliance system. That could become more important as governments and international organizations set clearer rules for which carbon removals can be used in regulated markets.

JAL Pairs Removals With SAF and Efficiency for Net Zero

JAL is not using carbon removals as its only way to cut aviation emissions. The airline says aircraft efficiency, operational improvements, and SAF remain priorities.

Noriko Ogawa, Executive Officer and Chairperson, Japan Airlines, noted:

“As the first airline to secure CORSIA-compliant carbon removals, we are proud to lead the industry toward net-zero emissions. While reducing emissions through aircraft renewal, operational innovations and the use of SAF remains our top priority, high-integrity carbon removals are essential to address residual emissions. Through this pioneering partnership with Climeworks, we aim to accelerate the adoption of high-quality solutions across international aviation and contribute to a sustainable future for air travel.”

JAL has set a target of reducing its FY2030 aircraft CO₂ emissions by 10% from FY2019 levels to 8.28 million metric tons. It also targets SAF equal to at least 10% of total fuel use by FY2030. JAL said SAF accounted for 1% of its fuel use in FY2025.

The airline has also used CORSIA-eligible credits.

JAL said in its latest sustainability disclosures that it met its FY2025 target of keeping net aircraft CO₂ emissions below its FY2019 level. The airline used several measures, including more fuel-efficient aircraft, operational improvements, SAF, and carbon credits.

The new agreement, therefore, adds carbon removals to a broader decarbonization strategy. It does not replace direct efforts to reduce aviation emissions.

DAC Adds a Longer-Term Carbon Removal Bet

The second part of the deal focuses on direct air capture. DAC uses machines to remove CO₂ directly from the air. The captured CO₂ can then be permanently stored, depending on the project and its storage method.

Climeworks operates the Mammoth DAC facility in Iceland. The company sees engineered carbon removal as a long-term way to deal with emissions that are difficult to eliminate.

JAL’s decision to buy Climeworks DAC credits alongside the broader CORSIA-focused portfolio gives the deal two different elements. The CORSIA-focused portfolio provides access to carbon removal methods designed around aviation’s compliance system.

The DAC purchases support a commercially scaling engineered carbon removal technology. These approaches, therefore, represent different parts of the growing carbon removal market.

A New Carbon Removal Market Takes Off in Aviation

The JAL-Climeworks deal does not mean that all carbon removals can now be used for CORSIA. Yet, the agreement shows that airlines are starting to look beyond traditional carbon offsets. They are also seeking carbon removal portfolios designed for specific compliance systems.

JAL and Climeworks call this deal the world’s first CORSIA-compliant carbon removal purchase agreement. The announcement does not establish that the credits have already been canceled for a CORSIA obligation. Still, the deal provides an early example of how carbon removals could move from the voluntary market into aviation’s regulated carbon market.

For carbon removal developers, the opportunity is to produce projects that meet increasingly detailed regulatory requirements. Airlines face the challenge of securing enough eligible units and the need to cut emissions. This can be done with more efficient aircraft, improved operations, and sustainable aviation fuel.

As CORSIA enters its second phase in 2027, these requirements could become an increasingly important source of demand for high-integrity carbon removal projects.

text:
Key Highlights

Tidewater Renewables Ltd. shares advanced 4.59% on September 21, extending positive momentum as investors reassessed the company's improving operating and financial trajectory.

Recent quarterly performance featured record adjusted operating profitability and exceptionally strong utilization at the company's renewable diesel and renewable hydrogen complex, prompting management to raise its full-year outlook.

Debt reduction, renewable-fuel hedging and progress toward a potential sustainable aviation fuel project provide additional strategic support, although Commodity pricing, regulation and project execution remain important risks.

Tidewater Renewables Ltd. (TSX:LCFS) is a Canadian energy-transition company focused on producing low-carbon fuels. Its portfolio includes renewable diesel and renewable hydrogen, alongside development opportunities in sustainable aviation fuel and other lower-carbon solutions. Improving plant utilization, stronger renewable-fuel margins and greater Earnings visibility have strengthened the company's operating narrative.

Why Did Tidewater Renewables Ltd. (TSX:LCFS) Rise by 4.59% on 21 September, 2026?

Tidewater Renewables shares closed 4.59% higher on September 21, continuing a strong upward sequence that had taken the shares materially above levels seen earlier in the month.

The constructive market response comes against an improving fundamental backdrop. In its latest quarterly update, Tidewater Renewables reported record adjusted operating profitability and record average throughput at its renewable diesel and renewable hydrogen complex. Management subsequently increased its full-year financial guidance, citing strong operating performance and a constructive Margin environment.

This combination of stronger utilization, improved margins and better earnings visibility appears supportive of the recent re-rating.

The Business model of Tidewater Renewables Ltd.

Tidewater Renewables produces low-carbon transportation fuels using renewable feedstocks such as waste oils, agricultural oils and other biomass-derived inputs.

Its flagship renewable diesel and renewable hydrogen complex converts these feedstocks into lower-carbon fuel products. Revenue generation is supported by physical renewable-fuel sales and environmental attributes associated with low-carbon production.

The company also uses longer-term offtake arrangements and hedging to reduce exposure to commodity-price volatility. Management previously reported that most forecast renewable diesel production for the current year was committed under offtake arrangements, with portions of future production also contracted.

Major Reasons Behind Upside

Operational improvement is one of the strongest elements supporting sentiment. During the latest reported quarter, the renewable diesel complex operated above its stated design capacity on an average-throughput basis, representing a substantial improvement from the comparative period.

Management also raised its full-year profitability guidance following stronger operational performance and favorable renewable-diesel margins. Regulatory developments surrounding renewable-fuel obligations have additionally supported the market environment for environmental credits and renewable diesel.

Balance-sheet improvement provides another positive factor. Tidewater Renewables reduced net Debt during the first half while emphasizing disciplined Capital allocation.

The sustainable aviation fuel opportunity could provide a longer-duration catalyst. The company entered a new initiative agreement with the Government of British Columbia to support pre-investment-decision work on its proposed SAF project, with a potential final Investment decision targeted later in 2026.

Geopolitical conditions are also relevant. Management has previously stated that Middle East conflict contributed to Volatility and stronger renewable-diesel benchmarks, while feedstock costs did not increase at the same pace, creating a more constructive margin environment.

What Are the Major Risks Investors Should Consider?

Commodity and margin volatility remain important risks. Renewable-diesel Economics depend on product pricing, feedstock costs and environmental-credit markets.

Regulatory exposure is also substantial because low-carbon fuel policies and renewable-fuel mandates influence industry economics. Changes in government incentives or environmental-credit frameworks could affect profitability.

Operational reliability at the company's main production complex remains essential. Unexpected outages or logistics constraints could reduce throughput.

The proposed sustainable aviation fuel development adds execution and funding risks. Moving from development work to construction would require disciplined capital allocation, regulatory progress and confidence in long-term project economics.

What Is the Dividend Outlook?

Tidewater Renewables currently has a stronger growth and balance-sheet optimization focus than an income-oriented profile.

Management's priorities include debt reduction, operational optimization and selective development of future renewable-fuel projects. Consequently, the investment proposition is presently more closely linked to cash-flow improvement and business expansion than regular dividend distributions.

How Does Tidewater Renewables Ltd. Compare With Other Industry Peers?

Tidewater Renewables offers relatively direct exposure to Canadian renewable-diesel production rather than the broader diversified operations typical of large conventional energy companies.

Its operating renewable diesel complex provides an advantage over development-stage clean-fuel businesses that have not yet reached commercial production.

The company also benefits from domestic renewable-fuel demand, environmental-credit mechanisms and existing infrastructure relationships. However, its comparatively concentrated asset base creates greater sensitivity to individual Facility performance than more diversified peers.

What Are the Bull and Bear Cases for TSX:LCFS?

Bull Case: Sustained high utilization, supportive renewable-diesel margins and disciplined hedging could strengthen cash generation. Further debt reduction could improve financial flexibility, while progress toward sustainable aviation fuel would potentially add another Long-term Growth platform.

Bear Case: Renewable-fuel margins could normalize if product prices weaken or feedstock costs rise. Changes to environmental regulations could reduce industry economics, while operational disruptions or expensive expansion projects could pressure cash flow.

Technical Levels to Watch

Support Zone: Recent breakout and consolidation areas could provide an initial support reference if short-term profit-taking emerges.

Resistance Levels: Recent trading highs may become important areas for determining whether momentum can continue.

Volume Trends: Investors should watch for sustained participation accompanying further upward sessions rather than relying solely on price appreciation.

Momentum Indicators: Short-term momentum appears constructive after consecutive gains, although the rapid advance increases the possibility of intermittent consolidation.

What Does the ESG Investment Case Look Like?

Tidewater Renewables' core business is directly associated with lowering the carbon intensity of transportation fuels. Renewable diesel can substitute for conventional diesel while utilizing renewable and waste-derived feedstocks.

Its proposed sustainable aviation fuel project could further broaden the company's role in transportation decarbonization.

Nevertheless, ESG investors must consider lifecycle emissions, feedstock sourcing, water and energy consumption and the sustainability characteristics of different renewable inputs. Governance around environmental credits, project investment and capital allocation is also important.

Outlook

Tidewater Renewables' outlook remains cautiously constructive. Operational performance has improved materially, management has raised guidance, and debt reduction is strengthening the financial profile.

Commercial arrangements and hedging provide additional earnings visibility, while the potential sustainable aviation fuel project offers a longer-term avenue for expansion.

The 4.59% advance on September 21 reflects improving investor sentiment, but maintaining that momentum will depend on continued plant reliability, favorable renewable-fuel economics and disciplined capital allocation. Regulatory conditions and geopolitical developments will also remain influential.

Asia Pacific Monthly Logistics Monitor: Road Freight Market at €1,693.6bn in 2025

Welcome to our latest Asia Pacific Logistics Monitor. Each month, as well as rounding up the most important events in the region, we showcase some of Ti’s exclusive research, data and analysis.

In this edition we draw on our Q3 2026 Ocean Freight Rate Tracker and the newly released road freight data in Ti’s Total Logistics Market Sizing 2026.

Ti’s Global Ocean Freight Headhaul Index reached 297.3 in July, the strongest quarterly increase since 2021, concentrated in the Asia-origin trades where carriers managed capacity most tightly. Headhaul rates out of China and East Asia reached US$6,729/FEU to the US West Coast and US$5,612/FEU to Europe, up 204.1% and 86.7% year on year. The backhaul legs sat at US$424 and US$552, a measure of how one-directional the region’s trade has become. Rates softened late in the quarter, so we expect firm but more balanced pricing in Q4.

Our newly released road freight market sizing values the Asia Pacific outsourced road freight market at €1,693.6bn in 2025, 45.7% of the global market and comfortably the region’s largest logistics segment. The market is expected to grow by 5.2% a year to €2,178.6bn by 2030, with India the standout at 8.5%. Asia Pacific total logistics is sized at €2,477.5bn, 43.6% of the global market.

For more detail and to buy the data, follow the links to the Q3 2026 Ocean Freight Rate Tracker and Ti’s Total Logistics Market Sizing 2026 on Ti Pro.

All our global reports cover the Asia Pacific region. As well as the quarterly rate trackers, see Global Freight Forwarding 2026, Global Contract Logistics 2026 and Datacentre Logistics 2026 for more in depth data and analysis.

What Ti’s analysts are writing about in the Asia Pacific market

Ningbo-Zhoushan has overtaken Singapore for the first time in Alphaliner’s Top 30, on 22.9m TEUs against 22.74m in H1 2026. Shanghai still leads on 28.7m. Further down, Colombo, Nhava Sheva and Jakarta are all growing by double digits as Gulf traffic reroutes.

De minimis reform is reshaping e-commerce air cargo. The EU’s new €3 per item charge has hit Asia to Europe lanes hardest, with Hong Kong to Europe volumes down 30% year on year in August. Airport throughput held up far better, so networks are rebalancing rather than losing demand.

COSCO has committed another US$3bn to newbuilds, taking its 2026 orders to 48 ships and close to US$8bn. The latest tranche pairs 22,000 TEU LNG dual-fuel tonnage for Asia to Northwest Europe with 3,200 TEU feeders, building the network in layers, not chasing scale.

The Chinese parcel market continues to grow, reaching 198.95bn items in 2025 and passing 100bn in the first half of 2026 alone. More striking is the return of profitability: SF Express grew Q1 net profit 10% on an 18.3% volume increase.

NYK’s Q1 results were driven by its energy business, with revenue up 21% and operating profit 69.8%, while liner and forwarding profits fell. CEO Takaya Soga notes that customers have absorbed longer routings and higher fuel costs without changing their booking behaviour.

Ares has raised a US$4bn fund for Japanese logistics real estate. Japan Logistics Development Partners V closed at ¥612bn with CPPIB as cornerstone investor, 50% larger than its predecessor and targeting Tokyo, Osaka and Nagoya.

Logistics M&A accelerated in August to 62 identified deals, with a consistent Asia Pacific thread. Investcorp bought 20Cube to build a pan-India contract logistics platform, SEFAS Group entered Indonesia, and two Australian transport businesses changed hands.

Fuel prices have entered dangerous territory, with Brent for November delivery at US$107 on 14 September, up around US$50 over the year. Jet fuel was 56.9% dearer in July than a year earlier. Asia Pacific operators pay that twice over, in bunkers and in air freight.

In other news:

The Pinglu Canal opened on 16 September under a one-year trial. The 134.2km waterway links Nanning in Guangxi to Qinzhou on the Beibu Gulf, takes vessels up to 5,000 tonnes and cuts more than 560km off the inland journey to the sea. Chinese authorities project logistics cost reductions of 18% to 30%.

CJ Logistics has launched THE FULFILL All-in-One, which the company says integrates B2B outbound shipment with B2C fulfilment in a single system, so Korean sellers need not split inventory between their own stores and marketplace channels. Its order management platform now takes direct feeds from 26 e-commerce platforms.

Sinotrans has flown its first route on a medical drone delivery line in Hebei province, through subsidiary TransTrans Hebei. The company says the operation is licensed by the Civil Aviation Administration of China and carries emergency medicines, test samples and consumables in temperature-controlled boxes.

Yusen Logistics has agreed to buy sustainable aviation fuel environmental attributes from Finnair on a book-and-claim basis, which separates the emissions benefit from the physical movement of fuel and cargo. No volumes or emissions figures were disclosed.

Amazon has signed its first standalone battery storage agreement globally, the 50MW Bairnsdale system in Victoria, and says it is the first non-energy company in Australia to do so. It now has 10 Australian battery projects totalling 368MW.

Logwin Air + Ocean has opened a branch in Lianyungang, its fourth in Jiangsu province, targeting the region’s chemicals, pharmaceuticals and life sciences base and the port’s rail connections.

text:
Praj Industries Ltd. (Pune, India) and Gevo, Inc.(Englewood, Colo.) announced the signing of a Development & Commercialization Agreement for Bio-Isobutanol (Bio-IBA) technology in India, reinforcing their long-standing association to advance sustainable low-carbon fuel solutions.

Under the agreement, Praj will lead the commercialization of Bio-IBA technology in India, with exclusive rights to deploy the technology in the country. The partnership will focus on developing commercial opportunities for Bio-IBA, with primary emphasis on diesel blending applications that have the potential to reduce the carbon intensity of one of the world’s most widely used transportation and industrial fuels.

The agreement builds upon more than a decade of association between the two companies to adapt, develop and advance Bio-IBA technology for Indian feedstocks and market requirements. Praj’s deep understanding of India’s sugar- and starch-based feedstocks, its expertise in engineering, project execution, scale-up and market development, combined with Gevo’s Bio-IBA technology, will support its scale-up and commercial adoption in India.

In a separate development aligned with the broader objective of advancing Bio-IBA adoption, Praj is currently establishing India’s first commercial Bio-IBA demonstration plant for a leading oil marketing company (OMC). The project is being designed, engineered, supplied and erected by Praj based on Gevo’s licensed Bio-IBA technology. The demonstration plant is expected to play an important role in validating production, supply-chain and market-development pathways for future commercialization opportunities in India.

Bio-IBA presents a promising opportunity for reducing the carbon footprint of diesel across a wide range of applications, including transportation, agriculture, mining, construction and industrial operations. Given India’s large diesel economy and abundant renewable feedstock resources, Bio-IBA has the potential to become an important component in the country’s transition toward lower-carbon fuels.

Encouragingly, stakeholders across the value chain, including fuel producers, vehicle and equipment manufacturers, research institutions and end users, are actively working toward enabling Bio-IBA-based diesel blending in India. Multiple initiatives aimed at technology validation, application development, regulatory assessment and supply-chain preparedness are progressing in parallel, reflecting growing industry interest in bringing diesel blending solutions to commercial reality.

“This agreement marks an important milestone in our relationship with Praj and in the advancement of Bio-IBA in India,” said Gevo Chief Executive Officer Paul Bloom. “Gevo brings proven renewable isobutanol technology and commercialization experience, while Praj contributes deep expertise in engineering, deployment and market development. Together, we are creating a framework to unlock new opportunities for Bio-IBA, particularly in diesel applications, while supporting broader decarbonization objectives.”

“Our collaboration with Gevo has steadily evolved through technology development, application innovation and market-building efforts over the years,” said Dr. Pramod Chaudhari, Founder Chairman, Praj Industries. “This Development & Commercialization Agreement establishes a strong foundation for bringing Bio-IBA to the Indian market. We believe Bio-IBA has the potential to emerge as an important renewable fuel solution for the diesel economy, complementing India’s broader energy transition and sustainability goals.”

Beyond diesel applications, Bio-IBA also serves as a platform molecule for the production of Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) and other renewable chemicals, further highlighting its versatility and long-term strategic importance within the emerging bioeconomy.

According to the Petroleum Planning & Analysis Cell (PPAC), India consumed approximately 94.7 million tons of high-speed diesel in FY2025-26, underscoring the significant opportunity for innovative low-carbon fuel solutions that can support the nation’s energy security and decarbonization ambitions.

AlphaCore 800 is designed to produce up to 800 barrels per day, or approximately 30 kt/a, of Fischer-Tropsch liquids from a single reactor.

text:
Velocys has expanded its Fischer-Tropsch reactor roadmap with AlphaCore 800, its highest-capacity microchannel FT reactor to date and a product designed specifically for the larger sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) and e-fuels projects now emerging globally.

AlphaCore 800 is designed to produce up to 800 barrels per day, or approximately 30 kt/a, of Fischer-Tropsch liquids from a single reactor. It extends the AlphaCore product family from approximately 50 to 800 barrels per day per reactor and is particularly suited to SAF plants targeting 100+ kt/a of production.

The objective behind the AlphaCore roadmap is straightforward: more FT capacity per reactor, enabling fewer reactors as project scale increases.

For project developers, reducing reactor count can simplify the Fischer-Tropsch island, reduce associated equipment requirements and lower FT unit cost while building on Velocys’ established microchannel technology platform and operating experience.

The effect becomes increasingly significant as projects grow. An FT unit requiring approximately 1,600 barrels per day, or 60 kt/a, of FT liquids could use two AlphaCore 800 reactors instead of eight AlphaCore 200 reactors, a 75% reduction in reactor count for the same FT liquids capacity.

AlphaCore 800 joins AlphaCore 50, 200 and 400 to create a throughput-based Fischer-Tropsch reactor family using the same core technology across multiple project scales and syngas pathways.

The new reactor is being announced as the sustainable fuels industry gathers in Hong Kong for Sustainable Aviation Futures China, where developers, technology providers and investors are considering the next generation of commercial-scale SAF and e-fuels projects across China and the wider Asian market.

text:
The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region delegation bagged four medals on Tuesday at the 20th Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, with swimming star Siobhan Haughey winning another gold.

As of 7 pm on Tuesday, the SAR had won 12 medals — three golds, five silvers and four bronzes — securing sixth place in the gold-medal standing and a tie for fourth in the overall medal tally.

Hong Kong sent about 580 athletes to compete in 38 events at the Asian Games, which began in mid-September and will run through Oct 4.

Haughey topped the women’s 100-meter freestyle event on Tuesday afternoon, bagging the third gold medal for the SAR delegation and her second gold at the tournament.

Haughey, who holds the event’s Asian record, reached the finishing line in 52.45 seconds, followed by Yu Yiting and Cheng Yujie of China’s national team.

Dubbed “the flying fish”, Haughey won a gold in the women’s 200m freestyle event on Monday, and a silver with the women’s 4x100m freestyle relay team. She will continue her medal-hunting journey in Thursday’s 50m freestyle event.

The SAR’s fencing team also made its debut on Tuesday, with foil fencer Ryan Choi Chun-yin, who holds seventh place in the world rankings, remaining unbeaten until the final, where he faced Japan’s world No 5-ranked Kazuki Iimura.

Iimura opened with four straight points, but Choi rallied to level at 12-12 before ultimately failing 13-15, taking his first Asian Games individual silver medal.

At the same event, Choi’s fellow fencer, two-time Olympic gold medalist Edgar Cheung Ka-long, was knocked out in the round of 32.

Wushu athlete Lau Chi-lung also secured a silver medal, with 19.456 points in the men’s Nanquan and Nangun event — the second wushu medal won by the SAR delegation.

Lau, 26, returned to the same event after finishing 11th in his Asian Games debut in Hangzhou, Zhejiang province, in 2023. He first scored 9.73 points in the Nanquan event to place third before adding 9.726 points in the subsequent Nangun competition.

Cyclist Chloe Leung Wing-yee clinched a bronze medal in the women’s road race event. The 90.4-kilometer race featured 40 competitors, including three from the SAR — Kwan Tsz-kwan, 25th place; and Guardiola Cheung Li-tong, 31st place.

text:
Global supply chain provider Yusen Logistics and Finnair Cargo have entered into a Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) agreement focused on the acquisition and allocation of SAF-related environmental attributes.

Facilitated with support from Western Associates, Inc. (WAI), Finnair’s General Sales Agent in Japan, the agreement creates a structured framework to reduce lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions associated with international air cargo operations.

Book-and-Claim Accounting and Scope 3 Reporting

The partnership leverages a Book-and-Claim accounting framework, decoupling the environmental attributes of SAF from physical fuel distribution and transport routing:

Book-and-Claim Mechanism: Enables Yusen Logistics to purchase SAF-related environmental attributes directly from Finnair, applying the carbon offset values across its global cargo forwarding footprint without altering physical flight routing or cargo handling workflows.

Emissions Verification and Scope 3 Transparency: Participating cargo shippers receive verified Scope 3 greenhouse gas emission reduction certificates and detailed audit reporting, allowing enterprise clients to document carbon reductions toward corporate ESG objectives.

Multi-Year Demand Commitment: Establishes a multi-year commercial commitment for voluntary SAF procurement, providing predictable demand signals to support long-term SAF production scale and market availability.

Executive Commentary

Gabriela Hiitola, Senior Vice President of Finnair Cargo, noted that creating long-term demand via enterprise SAF agreements accelerates the broader aviation energy transition and supports the expansion of renewable fuel supply chains.

Management at Yusen Logistics highlighted that the Book-and-Claim mechanism provides customers with clear Scope 3 emissions reporting while maintaining existing air freight schedules and service standards.

title: Almost a third of the EU's sustainable aviation fuel is supplied in the Netherlands
description:
In 2025, the Netherlands received more sustainable aviation fuel than any other EU member state.
Of the 1,1 million tonnes of Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) delivered to European airports, 320.000 tonnes ended up in the Netherlands.
This is evident from the new annual report on ReFuelEU Aviation by the European aviation agency EASA.
Fuel suppliers reported a total of 39,3 million tonnes of aviation fuel for 2025 at airports covered by the European scheme.
Spain followed with 152.000 tonnes, Germany with 116.000 tonnes, Italy with 111.000 tonnes, and France with 107.000 tonnes.
text:
In 2025, the Netherlands received more sustainable aviation fuel than any other EU member state. Of the 1,1 million tonnes of Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) delivered to European airports, 320.000 tonnes ended up in the Netherlands. At the same time, it appears that Europe is heavily dependent on raw materials from outside the European Union for the production of these fuels.

This is evident from the new annual report on ReFuelEU Aviation by the European aviation agency EASA. Fuel suppliers reported a total of 39,3 million tonnes of aviation fuel for 2025 at airports covered by the European scheme. Of this, 1,1 million tonnes, or 2,79 percent, consisted of SAF. This exceeded the European minimum obligation of 2 percent in the first year.

The amount of SAF increased sharply in a single year. In 2024, it amounted to 193.000 tonnes. In 2025, SAF was delivered to 121 airports in all 27 EU Member States. This represents 79 percent of the airports covered by the scheme.

The Netherlands on top

According to EASA, the Netherlands received 320.000 tonnes of SAF, accounting for 29 percent of the total reported amount in the European Union. Spain followed with 152.000 tonnes, Germany with 116.000 tonnes, Italy with 111.000 tonnes, and France with 107.000 tonnes. Schiphol was the European airport where the most SAF was delivered and also accounted for 29 percent of the European total.

In addition, the Netherlands plays an important role in imports. According to Eurostat data, approximately 173.000 tonnes of SAF were imported from outside the European Union in 2025, mainly via Dutch ports. These imports represented approximately 16 percent of the total amount of SAF delivered to European airports.

Raw materials mainly from outside Europe

Although 86 percent of the supplied SAF was produced within the European Union, 85 percent of the raw materials used came from outside the EU. China was by far the most important country of origin, at 61 percent. This was followed by Malaysia with 8 percent, Indonesia with 5 percent, and the United Kingdom with 3 percent. Only 15 percent of the raw materials came from the European Union.

Used frying oil was once again the main raw material and represented 80 percent of the supplied SAF. In addition, Category 3 animal fats, wastewater from palm oil mills, food waste, and crude tall oil, among others, were used. As a result, the share of advanced and other aviation biofuels increased.

3,77 million tons less greenhouse gas emissions

According to EASA, the SAF delivered in 2025 yielded a calculated lifecycle saving of 3,77 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent compared to the conventional aviation fuel it replaced. On average, the reduction amounted to 89 percent. In 2024, the calculated saving was still 714.000 tonnes of CO2 equivalent.

This does not mean that no CO2 is released when SAF is burned in an aircraft engine. The calculated reduction relates to greenhouse gas emissions over the life cycle of the fuel.

Production towards 2030

Under ReFuelEU Aviation, the mandatory share of SAF will rise to 6 percent in 2030. EASA expects that European production capacity may be sufficient to meet that share, provided that planned production projects are actually realized.

With only the production capacity already available at the end of 2025, Europe could produce approximately 1,5 million tonnes of SAF in 2030. When installations under construction and projects with a final investment decision are also included, the potential capacity rises to 3,7 million tonnes. EASA emphasizes that this concerns potential capacity and not guaranteed production.

The Netherlands is among the eight EU countries that already had at least one facility capable of producing SAF by the end of 2025. The other countries were Austria, Finland, France, Germany, Italy, Spain, and Sweden.

First full year

The figures for 2025 relate to the first full year in which the main obligations of ReFuelEU Aviation applied. Of the 115 fuel suppliers subject to the reporting obligation, 102 submitted data. EASA therefore warns that the reported 1,1 million tonnes does not necessarily include all SAF supplied in the European Union in 2025.

Source: EASA, ReFuelEU Aviation Annual Technical Report 2026

text:
OMV Petrom, the largest integrated energy producer in Southeastern Europe, is advancing the construction of the new sustainable fuels production unit at Petrobrazi. This EUR 560 million investment will position the refinery as the first major producer of sustainable fuels in the region. The foundations have been laid, and the main equipment for processing sustainable fuels - including columns and reactors - has been mounted and installed. With a capacity of 250,000 metric tons per year, the new unit will produce sustainable aviation fuel and renewable diesel, fuels that can contribute to reducing emissions in hard-to-electrify sectors such as aviation and heavy transport.

“Petrobrazi is going through one of the most important transformations in its recent history. With a EUR 560 million investment, we are building a new unit that will produce 250,000 metric tons per year of sustainable fuels made from renewable feedstocks. These lower carbon fuels will contribute to reducing emissions in sectors where electrification is difficult, such as aviation and heavy transport. We have completed the foundations, for which approximately 20,000 cubic meters of concrete were poured, and equipment up to 60 meters high is already installed in the refinery. This is a project through which we are gradually adapting Petrobrazi to the new requirements of the market and of the energy transition, including through the development of sustainable fuels production,” said Radu Căprău, member of the OMV Petrom Executive Board.

text:
California has moved closer to making E15, a fuel blend containing 15% ethanol, available to motorists after Governor Gavin Newsom signed legislation removing a regulatory hurdle for its sale in the state, Energy.Agwired reported.

Newsom signed Senate Bill 795, known as the “E15 Clean-up Act”, over the weekend after the California Legislature unanimously passed the measure on August 31. The legislation addresses an equipment-related regulatory issue linked to last year’s Assembly Bill 30, which authorised the sale of E15 in California.

The new law allows fuel retailers to use existing vapor recovery equipment to dispense E15, provided the equipment manufacturer submits a statement confirming its compatibility to the relevant state agencies, according to the Renewable Fuels Association (RFA).

Newsom said the measure would give consumers another fuel option while helping diversify California’s fuel supply. He also said the legislation removes unnecessary regulatory barriers while retaining existing environmental and safety standards.

The RFA welcomed the governor’s decision. RFA President and CEO Geoff Cooper said the legislation brings California closer to offering motorists E15 and the potential fuel-cost and environmental benefits associated with higher ethanol blends.

The association also credited Senators Bob Archuleta and Suzette Martinez Valladares, Assemblymember David Alvarez and members of the bipartisan California Problem Solvers Caucus for their role in advancing the legislation.

With SB 795 now signed into law, California has removed a key regulatory obstacle to the rollout of E15, paving the way for retailers to use compatible existing infrastructure to supply the ethanol blend.

“As the world’s number one cargo operator at the world’s busiest cargo airport, we remain committed to continuing to grow our business and reinforcing Hong Kong’s status as a world-leading international aviation hub.
